notice: This unpublished synthetic assignment contains a disclosed first-attempt training rejection for the second full-batch item before model dispatch. It is not a real provider outage. Only actual saved pilot, per-item and retry receipts establish what occurred; no staff review, credit or external delivery is involved.
task: Use one owned extraction and all three assigned proposals. Inspect a two-document pilot, justify the model and bounded scale-up from its source-checked results, account for every input in the actual batch, then recover only the confirmed failed item while preserving the original successful results.
instructions: Create or select your own extraction with exactly the five named fields. Capture its exact instructions and all three complete assigned PDFs; matching filenames or a count of three cannot substitute for owned assigned identities.

Inspect the saved model configuration and complete sources. Explain why proposals 1 and 3 provide a useful bounded pilot, and why their shared layout does not establish general reliability on other sponsors, formats or scans. Explicitly approve only this pilot before running it.

Inspect all ten actual pilot values against the original sources. A completed run or consistency badge does not establish source correctness. If values are wrong, repair the extraction and run a new pilot before considering the complete batch; retain earlier results.

After a complete source-supported pilot, record your quality/resource tradeoff and approve the exact same revision and model for all three assigned proposals. Use actual elapsed time and available measurements; leave token usage, price and wider generalizations unknown when not measured.

Run the complete approved batch. The second item is deliberately rejected before model dispatch on this first full-batch attempt. Inspect each actual terminal receipt and its assigned document ID, including failures. Terminal inventory coverage is distinct from usable successful coverage.

Inspect the saved confirmed failure and verify its source, original batch and unchanged extraction settings. The training gate permits one explicitly approved attempt of that failed item. Preserve every successful original item; never launch the entire batch again as a recovery shortcut. Unknown or in-flight outcomes require reading the original receipt first.

After the targeted retry, reconcile the three assigned input IDs with their original or linked retry receipts and inspect all fifteen source-supported values. Retain the original failure. Explain actual recovery, remaining exceptions and the pilot limitations without claiming a larger production rollout or external delivery.
exclusions: Use only the three assigned synthetic proposals; no real institutional or sponsor data is required.
No email, workspace sharing, external write or staff review is part of this assignment.
A count, an unrelated historical batch, an invented price estimate or a model assurance cannot award credit.

pilot_limitations: Proposals 1 and 3 exercise different principal investigators, budgets and research areas within this small assigned set. All three proposals use one template and one sponsor; this pilot does not establish quality on other layouts, sponsors, scanned documents or larger workloads.

questions.prompt: Explain why these two complete proposals and this configured model are appropriate for a bounded pilot. Identify the five source values you will check, permitted data scope and limitations of the shared layout before approving execution.

Cite actual pilot values, source checks, elapsed time and configured models. Explain the quality/resource tradeoff and why you approve or hold the three-document batch. Keep unmeasured token cost and broader reliability unknown.

Identify the original batch and confirmed failed document, the saved failure and what was or was not dispatched. Explain why retrying only this item is justified and which completed receipts must remain untouched.

Reconcile every assigned document with its original or linked retry result. Explain the original failure, preserved successful items, actual source quality, remaining exceptions and pilot limitations. Distinguish terminal coverage from successful usable results.

passing_conditions: The intended batch accounts for every assigned input ID and each terminal result; counts alone do not establish coverage.
critical_failures: Use an unrelated historical batch, repeated input or documents-touched count as proof.
review_guidance.case_application: Use deterministic exact assigned-document IDs, source hashes, artifact revision and the original batch receipt inventory. Each input must have its own terminal result; preserve the difference between completed, failed and uncertain. No model opinion can fill a missing item or replace an original batch with historical counts.

passing_conditions: The retry is tied to the failed input and original run; successful outputs and completed side effects are preserved.
critical_failures: Blindly retry the entire batch or hide unresolved failures behind an overall success label.
review_guidance.case_application: Bind the learner recovery choice to the actual confirmed failed original item and its explicit retry receipt. Verify original successful receipt hashes are unchanged and the retry targets no successful or unknown item. Preserve the disclosed controlled training rejection without misrepresenting it as a real outage or erased failure.

passing_conditions: The learner uses representative pilot evidence and records the quality/resource tradeoff before scaling.
critical_failures: Treat the cheapest or fastest execution as sufficient regardless of missing or wrong results.
review_guidance.case_application: Use the actual complete two-case pilot, its source checks, exact configured model and elapsed-time evidence. Require a learner decision before scaling the same revision and sources. Reject fabricated price or usage claims, universal quality claims from the shared template, and speed-only justification despite unsupported pilot values.
